exposure: early-term delivery (37 0/7 to 38 6/7 weeks of gestation)
full-term delivery (39 0/7 to 41 6/7 weeks of gestation)
cohort: Infants born between January 2013 and December 2014 at a tertiary center in Turkey, categorized as early-term (37 0/7 to 38 6/7 weeks) or full-term (39 0/7 to 41 6/7 weeks) gestation.
finding: Early-term infants experience significantly higher rates of various neonatal morbidities, including NICU admission, respiratory distress, jaundice, hypoglycemia, feeding difficulty, and dehydration, compared to full-term infants.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rates were significantly higher in early-term infants.
cross-section timing: Infants born between January 2013 and December 2014
gest_age: Early-term (37 0/7 to 38 6/7 weeks of gestation) and full-term (39 0/7 to 41 6/7 weeks of gestation)
